newsitem.title: USA: Muni ylds rise 5 basis points over week -- Delphis.
newsitem.headline: Muni ylds rise 5 basis points over week -- Delphis.

text.p: Municipal bond yields rose an average of five basis points in the week ended Thursday, Delphis Hanover Corp. said Friday.
Yields have been on a steady upward course for several weeks, following the Treasury market higher.
But munis this week underperformed the government market, as the yield on the Treasury's 30-year bond remained unchanged for the week at 6.96 percent.
Thirty-year, Aaa-rated municipal yields, in contrast, rose five basis points to 5.75 percent, after rising 10 the week before. Thirty-year Baa yields also rose five basis points to 6.55 percent.
Thirty-year, Aaa-rated munis were yielding 82.6 percent of the Treasury long bond at the close Thursday, rising from 81.9 percent the week before and 81.4 percent earlier in the month.
Average yields on one-year municipal bonds rose five basis points across the credit spectrum for the second week in a row, rising to 3.75 percent in the Aaa category and 4.60 percent for Baa's.
Yields also rose five basis points in the intermediate sector for the second consecutive week, moving ten-year Aaa-rated bonds to five percent and Baa-rated ten-years to 5.85 percent.
The triple-A yield curve between one-year and 30-year bonds was unchanged at 200 basis points, after steepening five basis points the week before. The Baa curve also held steady, at 195 basis points.
The credit spread between Aaa-rated and Baa-rated one-years was unchanged for the second consecutive week at 85 basis points, and the 30-year spread was also steady at 80 basis points.
